absent: Numeric values and bit layout of follower options, fault options, fault status words, and marker encodings.
Memory layout of address space, area, table entry, folio, huge state, and file mapping structures.
Semantics of table walk, huge allocation, cache maintenance, and architecture permission helpers.
Behavior of the ordinary fault path and the huge allocation and copy and unmap and userfault delegation paths.
Locking contracts for the address space lock and area and folio and table locks beyond ordering shown.
Side effects of accounting and resource control and least recently used tracking and notifier calls.
Derivation of huge boundaries and masks and offsets and state selection from area configuration.
Failure modes of folio reference acquisition and zero page identification and reservation map updates.

findings.text: The symbol handle_mm_fault is available to other parts of the kernel as the general fault entry, accepting an area plus address plus options plus register context and reporting a fault status.
The symbol hugetlb_fault is available to other parts of the kernel as the huge page fault entry, accepting an address space plus area plus address plus options and reporting a fault status.
The symbol restore_reserve_on_error is available to other parts of the kernel to reconcile per area reservation state with folio restore intent after a failed huge page operation.

The general fault entry normalizes caller options, refuses accesses forbidden by architecture policy, establishes resource tracking context for user faults, delegates huge page areas to the huge handler and other areas to the ordinary handler, treats resource exhaustion as nonfatal for droppable areas, and records accounting before returning. Callers must assume the area descriptor may have been released during handling.

The huge page fault entry aligns the faulting address to the huge page boundary, serializes concurrent instantiation for the same file offset through a hashed mutex, secures shared area access while allocating and examining the huge table entry, and selects among allocation, marker, migration wait, poison, userfault, copy on write, and access flag update outcomes.

Gate area lookup refuses FOLL_WRITE, requires each upper table level and the leaf entry to be populated, and reports fault when any level is missing. Ordinary entries resolve through vm_normal_page while the shared zero case is accepted only when FOLL_DUMP is absent, and success follows acquisition through try_grab_folio.

The helper that forces a page into place rejects FOLL_NOFAULT and maps remaining follower intent to corresponding fault indications for write, remote, retry behavior, and unshare, expanding unlockable and nonwaiting into retry related fault modes with interruptible available only as an opt in. Unshare via FAULT_FLAG_UNSHARE is treated as incompatible with write.

Areas carrying VM_DROPPABLE have VM_FAULT_OOM suppressed to nonfatal, and memory control out of memory synchronization is performed only when no exhaustion remains reported. The area descriptor must not be used after delegation because the address space lock may have been dropped and the area released.

Huge entries holding markers distinguish PTE_MARKER_POISONED, which reports large poison tagged with the huge state index, from guard, which is unsupported and reports segmentation failure, while other markers take the allocation path. Nonpresent nonempty entries either wait for migration to complete and report success or report large poison.

Protection none huge entries in accessible areas with read write tracking enabled and with the userfault indicator present are treated as tracking faults for VM_UFFD_RWP. The synchronous configuration delegates to the userfault handler after releasing huge locks, while the asynchronous configuration updates protection under the huge table lock, clears the tracking indicator, marks youth, refreshes the cache, and reports success.

When a write or unshare fault reaches an area lacking VM_MAYSHARE through a nonwritable huge entry, reservation need is evaluated before acquiring the table lock. Lack of reservation reports resource exhaustion, otherwise the reservation count is adjusted without deallocation.

Write faults to huge entries that carry the userfault indicator in areas with write protection tracking take the userfault path before further locking. The synchronous configuration releases all huge locks and delegates for VM_UFFD_WP, while the asynchronous configuration clears the indicator in place and continues toward copy on write.

Ending and deleting per area huge reservations both delegate to a shared reservation helper with VMA_END_RESV and VMA_DEL_RESV. Repair after failure reconciles current reservation need against the folio restore marking, adding, ending, deleting, or preserving reserve state and setting or clearing the restore marking to keep global accounting consistent when reserve map updates fail for lack of memory.

Forced fault outcomes form a small machine where completed faults drop the held lock state and request the caller to acquire again, error reports map to a process error or an internal inconsistency, retry reports drop the held lock state except in nonwaiting mode and request a busy retry, and absence of those indications means success.

Huge copy on write prefers in place reuse for exclusively mapped anonymous folios, marking exclusivity and making the entry writable when sharing is not being dissolved. Otherwise it moves through folio acquisition, anonymous preparation, content copy, invalidation notification, revalidation, and installation, with distinct failure exits for allocation failure, preparation failure, copy poisoning, and racing updates.

When folio acquisition fails for the reserve owner of a private mapping, the helper releases area and fault serialization, removes references held by other users of the private mapping, reacquires serialization and the table lock, rewalks the entry, and retries reuse when the entry is unchanged. A changed entry ends the operation as complete because another party has progressed the mapping.

Huge fault serialization orders the hashed fault mutex before shared area access before the huge table spinlock, with anonymous folio locking attempted only while holding the table lock. Blocking paths release the fault mutex and area access before waiting or delegating to userfault handling, and the table lock is released before returning, with folio wait performed outside all huge locks when the try lock fails.

The huge copy on write helper expects the table spinlock held on entry, releases it across allocation and copy and notifier windows, reacquires it to revalidate the entry before installation, and returns with it held. The owner reclaim window additionally releases area access and fault serialization across unmapping and reacquires them before rewalking.

Gate lookup holds a leaf mapped via pte_offset_map only while sampling the entry and resolving the page, releasing via pte_unmap on every exit including fault, missing page, and reference acquisition failure.

The huge fault descriptor carries vma with address aligned to the huge boundary with real_address preserving the original with flags holding options with pgoff holding the file offset, while pte with ptl with orig_pte are populated after allocation and sampling. Certain members stay unset and callees must not assume their presence.

Requesting unshare together with write is diagnosed as a programming error. Observing a completed fault while in nonwaiting retry mode is diagnosed as unexpected. An error report that maps to no process error is treated as an internal inconsistency.

Huge fault and copy paths resample the table entry under the table lock and compare for sameness before modifying access state or installing a new folio. Mismatch causes the operation to be abandoned without installation, leaving progress to a later fault.
The helpers use EFAULT for hard failure with EBUSY for retry with EAGAIN for lock reacquire and zero for success.

Fault dispatch uses VM_FAULT_ERROR with VM_FAULT_RETRY with VM_FAULT_COMPLETED with VM_FAULT_SIGSEGV with VM_FAULT_OOM with VM_FAULT_HWPOISON_LARGE, the poison case carrying the huge state index via VM_FAULT_SET_HINDEX.
